sammamish-river-trail.name: Sammamish River Trail
sammamish-river-trail.description: A beautiful 10.1-mile paved path that runs along the Sammamish River from Bothell to Marymoor Park in Redmond. This popular trail offers stunning views of the river, surrounding wetlands, and forested areas.
sammamish-river-trail.features: Scenic river views, wildlife viewing, picnic areas, restrooms, parking
sammamish-river-trail.surface: Paved trail suitable for walking, running, cycling, and skating
accessPoints: Wilmot Gateway Park: 17301 131st Ave NE, Woodinville, WA 98072
Blyth Park: 16950 W Riverside Dr, Bothell, WA 98011
Marymoor Park: 6046 W Lake Sammamish Pkwy NE, Redmond, WA 98052
sammamish-river-trail.bestTimes: Year-round, with peak season from spring through fall. Early morning and evening offer the best wildlife viewing opportunities.

tolt-macdonald-park.name: Tolt-MacDonald Park
tolt-macdonald-park.description: A beautiful park featuring the iconic suspension bridge over the Snoqualmie River, offering stunning views and recreational opportunities.
tolt-macdonald-park.features: Suspension bridge, river views, hiking trails, picnic areas, camping
tolt-macdonald-park.surface: Mixed surfaces including paved and natural trails
accessPoints: Main entrance: 31020 NE 40th St, Carnation, WA 98014
tolt-macdonald-park.bestTimes: Year-round, with beautiful fall colors and spring wildflowers

st-edward-state-park.name: Saint Edward State Park
st-edward-state-park.description: A historic state park featuring the former Saint Edward Seminary, beautiful forest trails, and stunning views of Lake Washington.
st-edward-state-park.features: Historic seminary building, forest trails, lake views, picnic areas
st-edward-state-park.surface: Natural forest trails with some paved sections
accessPoints: Main entrance: 14445 Juanita Dr NE, Kenmore, WA 98028

snoqualmie-falls.name: Snoqualmie Falls
snoqualmie-falls.description: One of Washington's most popular attractions, featuring a spectacular 268-foot waterfall. The viewing area offers breathtaking views and there are several trails for hiking around the area.
snoqualmie-falls.features: 268-foot waterfall, observation deck, gift shop, hiking trails, historic lodge
snoqualmie-falls.surface: Paved viewing areas with natural hiking trails
accessPoints: Main parking and observation deck: 6200 Fish Hatchery Rd SE, Snoqualmie, WA 98065
snoqualmie-falls.bestTimes: Year-round, but spring and winter offer the most dramatic water flow. Fall provides beautiful foliage.

rattlesnake-lake.name: Rattlesnake Lake
rattlesnake-lake.description: A beautiful alpine lake surrounded by towering mountains and old-growth forest. Popular for easy family hikes, picnicking, and stunning mountain reflections in the water.
rattlesnake-lake.features: Alpine lake, mountain views, picnic areas, restrooms, easy hiking trails, old-growth forest
rattlesnake-lake.surface: Easy gravel trail around the lake
accessPoints: Main parking area: End of Rattlesnake Lake Road, North Bend, WA 98045
rattlesnake-lake.bestTimes: Year-round, with summer and fall being most popular. Spring offers wildflowers, winter can be muddy.

twin-falls.name: Twin Falls Trail
twin-falls.description: A moderate hike leading to spectacular twin waterfalls cascading down rocky cliffs. The trail follows the South Fork Snoqualmie River through beautiful old-growth forest.
twin-falls.features: Twin waterfalls, river views, old-growth forest, wooden bridges, rocky pools
twin-falls.surface: Natural forest trail with some rocky sections and wooden bridges
accessPoints: Trailhead parking: End of SE 159th Street, North Bend, WA 98045
twin-falls.bestTimes: Best from late spring through fall. Winter and early spring can be muddy and icy.

paradise-valley-conservation-area.name: Paradise Valley Conservation Area
paradise-valley-conservation-area.description: A beautiful 793-acre conservation area featuring mature second-growth forest, wetlands, and over 13 miles of designated multi-use trails. This park plays a vital role in the health of the Bear Creek watershed and offers trails for all fitness levels.
paradise-valley-conservation-area.features: Multi-use trails, forest, wetlands, wildlife viewing, mountain biking, equestrian trails
paradise-valley-conservation-area.surface: Natural trails suitable for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding
accessPoints: Main trailhead: 23210 Paradise Lake Road, Woodinville, WA 98077
paradise-valley-conservation-area.bestTimes: Year-round, with spring and fall offering the best conditions. Early morning provides excellent wildlife viewing.

rotary-community-park.name: Rotary Community Park
rotary-community-park.description: Woodinville's largest community park established in 2001, featuring a half-mile boardwalk loop trail through the woods, playground facilities, and diverse recreational amenities for families.
rotary-community-park.features: Boardwalk trail, playground, climbing boulder, skate park, picnic areas, wetland areas
rotary-community-park.surface: Boardwalk and paved paths suitable for all ages
accessPoints: Main entrance: 19518 136th Avenue NE, Woodinville, WA 98072
rotary-community-park.bestTimes: Spring through fall for best weather conditions. Year-round accessibility.

juanita-bay-park.name: Juanita Bay Park
juanita-bay-park.description: A stunning 110-acre urban wildlife habitat featuring over 200 bird species, beavers, and diverse flora. The park offers 3,000 feet of trails and boardwalks through six different plant communities including marshlands and open water areas.
juanita-bay-park.features: Wildlife viewing, boardwalks, bird watching, wetlands, Forbes Creek access
juanita-bay-park.surface: Boardwalks and natural trails, wheelchair accessible
accessPoints: Main entrance: 2201 Market Street, Kirkland, WA 98033
juanita-bay-park.bestTimes: Year-round, with spring and fall offering peak wildlife viewing. Early morning is best for bird watching.

cottage-lake-park.name: Cottage Lake Park
cottage-lake-park.description: A scenic 20-acre park surrounding a beautiful lake, offering a perfect combination of water activities and hiking trails. Features a floating dock, swimming pool operated by Northshore YMCA, and loop trail with boardwalk sections along the lake.
cottage-lake-park.features: Lake access, floating dock, swimming pool, playground, boat launch, kayak access, picnic shelter
cottage-lake-park.surface: Paved path transitioning to boardwalk along the lake
accessPoints: Main entrance: 18831 Northeast Woodinville Duvall Road, Woodinville, WA 98072
cottage-lake-park.bestTimes: Year-round for hiking, spring through fall for water activities and swimming
